measurement: alignment between the release and pre-fix H3 tokenizers on one prompt

id_provenance.core_comment_says: ids fixed by the released tokenizer
id_provenance.evidence_class: SOURCE. The config assigns no id as a literal, but loading the release's own tokenizer directory with the standard HF loader yields 151669-151675 and tokenizes the seven as single tokens. The ids are fixed by construction from the shipped config, so core's comment is correct and release_id addresses the rows the vendor's own pipeline would address.
id_provenance.worry_this_closes: raised twice, on 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-27: that core DERIVED the numbering and might have guessed wrong, which would mean every marker arm addresses arbitrary rows. It did not guess. Recorded here so the third session to notice the missing literal finds the answer instead of re-raising it.

index_wise_is_misleading: reported only to retire it. An insertion shifts every later index, so this counts displacement as if it were content change. Use longest_common_subsequence. A record of this repo's carried the index-wise number alone and it read as 'the tokenizations are wildly different', which the alignment refutes.
what_it_does_not_settle: whether legacy_bpe's prediction delta comes from the changed content or from the displacement. Both are present and this sizes them; separating them needs a padding arm that reproduces the displacement with content untouched, specified by edit_sites.

marker_id_reach.question: which of the seven marker ids do our surfaces actually carry

calibration_and_holdout_bundles.bundle_v2_Bp2: 15 of 29 rows carry 151669/151670; the other five ids in zero rows
calibration_and_holdout_bundles.pool: <d>/</d> in 505 rows, the other five in 0 (2026-08-25_v3_selection_max_no_upscale.json)

marker_id_reach.shipped_graphs: <d>/</d> in 23 of 137; the other five in none
marker_id_reach.marker_corpus: all seven present (bench/marker_corpus/compiled.json) -- the only surface that reaches them
marker_id_reach.consequence: every encoder measurement this repo has taken -- Gate 5, the overfit test, the four-encoder table -- exercises 2 of the 7 markers, because they all run on these bundles. The five are not mis-tokenized; they are absent. Claims about 'the encoder's handling of H3 markers' from those runs cover <d> and </d> only.
marker_id_reach.where_it_could_bite: AWQ targets Linear, so embed_tokens is untouched and layer0_input relL2 is exactly 0.0 -- the marker ROWS are bit-identical in v1/v2. NVFP4 is the exception: it ships the embedding table at I8, so it does perturb all seven rows, and five of them have never appeared in any population it was graded on.
